frontier.name: Coefficient-valued classification
frontier.text: : extend the scalar result to H²_cont(g((t)), Z) ≃ Z for an arbitrary discrete Z by constructing the normalising continuous coboundary without finite-dimensionality. A2's universal property depends on this.

frontier.name: Topology and splitting of ĝκ
frontier.text: : give the residue extension its continuous inclusion, projection and section. Then classify continuously split central extensions with one-dimensional discrete kernel and prove universality.

frontier.name: The dual Coxeter number
frontier.text: : define h∨ intrinsically and prove Killing = 2h∨κ0, building on the invariant-form uniqueness already proved. This fixes the critical level κc = −h∨κ0.

frontier.name: Central-level UEA and its completion (A4)
frontier.text: : form Uκ by the relation ι(K) = 1, the left ideals I_N and the inverse limit Ûκ with its multiplication. The A5 smooth-module equivalence and everything centre-related wait on this.

frontier.name: Affine loop lifts
frontier.text: : lift Ad_g to ĝκ with the residue Maurer–Cartan term. This needs the pinned G((t)) and the Maurer–Cartan differential from FormalConnectionsOpers.

status.glance: The core of A1 is proved: the continuous second cohomology of formal loops is classified by invariant forms. A2 and A5 are each partly built. A3, A4 and A6–A8 have not begun, so neither headline theorem has been started. Those are the scalar center away from critical level and Feigin–Frenkel.

frontier.name: Maximum principle on compact submanifolds (A1)
frontier.text: — show that no compact positive-dimensional complex submanifold carries a strictly plurisubharmonic restriction. A3's dimension bound and A5's component argument both use it.

frontier.name: Projective carrier topology (A0)

frontier.name: Smooth locus at full Jacobian rank (A0)
frontier.text: — from the existing rank lemmas, construct the induced complex submanifold of dimension N−1−|ι| and its tangent/normal sequence. This needs K7's holomorphic submanifold API.

frontier.name: Affine CW dimension ≤ n (A2)
frontier.text: — move the flat shape-operator and squared-distance results onto the GT Layer1 normal carrier and R6's intrinsic shape operator. Then combine properness, almost-everywhere Morse genericity and MorseTheory M1–M2.

frontier.name: Pseudoconvex exhaustion topology (A3)
frontier.text: — Morse-approximate a strongly q-pseudoconvex exhaustion using fine C² openness to get a CW model of dimension ≤ n+q. This depends on MorseTheory M3–M4.

status.glance: A1, the Levi calculus and the real index bounds, is done except for the maximum principle on compact submanifolds. frontier.name: Relative Hurewicz and homological Whitehead
frontier.text: — surjectivity of the relative Hurewicz map is proved ([`TauCeti.RelHomotopyGroup.surjective_hurewicz`](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Homotopy/Hurewicz/Relative.html#TauCeti.RelHomotopyGroup.surjective_hurewicz)). Injectivity is proved only when both spaces are `(n−1)`-connected, and is still needed when `A` and `X` are merely simply connected. Homological Whitehead then follows using the mapping cylinder.

frontier.name: Pinning the Hurewicz sign
frontier.text: — the classical and cubical Hurewicz maps are known to agree only up to a universal unit of `ℤ`. The roadmap's orientation conventions ask for that sign to be fixed.

frontier.name: Serre spectral sequence
frontier.text: — the spectral sequence of a filtered space exists, and fibre bundles give Serre fibrations. What remains is the skeletal filtration of the total space and `E² = H_p(B; H_q(F))` with monodromy. Euler multiplicativity for bundles waits on it.

frontier.name: Fundamental classes and Poincaré duality
frontier.text: — the compact simply connected case gives `Hₙ(M) ≅ R`. The integral fundamental class of an oriented compact manifold, both forms of duality, and the linking pairing remain.

frontier.name: Algebraic spectral sequences
frontier.text: — the hereditary-ring Künneth and universal coefficient theorems are done. The general-ring Künneth Tor, universal-coefficient Ext and Cartan–Leray spectral sequences are absent.

status.glance: Van Kampen, relative singular homology, and excision with Mayer–Vietoris (Stages 1–3) are done. The absolute Hurewicz theorem, Whitehead's theorem, Künneth and universal coefficients over hereditary rings, and the homology of projective spaces are proved. Relative Hurewicz is proved only in a special case. Manifold duality, homological Whitehead, and every spectral sequence except the Čech one are still missing.

status.glance: Every layer of the roadmap is now done. A finite regular fan has a Hausdorff complex manifold with a holomorphic torus action, the orbit–cone correspondence, and a normal-crossings boundary. Its fan morphisms give holomorphic toric maps, with a properness criterion that covers star subdivisions. The realization is torus-equivariantly biholomorphic to the complex points of the fan scheme, and the README's standard examples, from affine and projective space to a blow-up, are worked out. No milestone named in the README is left open.

frontier.name: Separating ideals (A5)
frontier.text: : show that the separating space of a surjective homomorphism, or of a module-intertwining map, is a separating ideal. The stability lemma this needs is now in place.

frontier.name: Rickart's theorem (A1)
frontier.text: : prove that the norm on a simple Banach module is unique up to equivalence and that module endomorphisms are scalars, via Gelfand–Mazur. The existence of a complete norm is done, in the unital case.

frontier.name: Primitive ideals and the radical (A1)
frontier.text: : maximal modular left ideals, primitive ideals, the radical as their intersection, and semisimplicity of the quotient. A5's structure theorem depends on these.

frontier.name: Cohen–Hewitt for right modules and bimodules (A4)
frontier.text: : this includes pseudo-unitality of essential bimodules. The left-module construction should transfer, after which dual actions and Arens products open up.

frontier.name: Holomorphic functional calculus (A2)
frontier.text: : the next prerequisite is the finite-cycle and grid construction around compact subsets of open sets, which disconnected spectra require.

status.glance: Four of the eight layers are under way and none is finished. A4 has its depth milestone, Cohen–Hewitt factorization, for left modules. A5 has the separating space and the stability lemma but none of its continuity theorems. A1 has the radical, and A2 has its Banach-valued Cauchy theory, but not the functional calculus. A3, A6, A7 and A8 have not begun.

frontier.name: Grothendieck's inequality
frontier.text: — the finite Gaussian model and the truncation argument with `κ_ℝ = 8`. Its operator corollaries also need B5's `L∞ ≃ C(K_μ)`, which has not begun.

frontier.name: The Cartan–Poincaré converse
frontier.text: — the README asks that linearity be *equivalent* to the graded Cartan and Poincaré series being inverse under `q ↦ -q`. Only the forward direction is proved. The single-variable identity cannot see Ext off the diagonal, and the source says outright that it does not claim the converse. For quadratic algebras, "numerically Koszul" is known not to imply Koszul, so the target looks unprovable as stated. The bigraded criterion, which is proved, is the natural replacement, and the README should be amended to match.

frontier.name: Non-split degree-zero parts
frontier.text: — the graded projective basis, graded unimodularity and the conjugate-transpose relation are proved only when the degree-zero part is spanned by orthogonal idempotents. A version that keeps the `dim_k End(Sᵢ)` factors, as the ungraded Layer 4 does, is not established here.

status.glance: Every layer except Layer 3 is done, and so are all five worked examples. The graded quiver comparison is closed in both its Cartan and its Ext halves. Layer 3 lacks only one direction of one equivalence: getting from the Cartan–Poincaré identity back to linear resolutions. As the README states it, that direction looks unprovable.

frontier.text: : torsion as an alternating product of projected minors, and additivity under direct sums. Both are needed before torsion can be taken componentwise.

frontier.name: Total quotient rings (N4)
frontier.text: : show that the total quotients of ℤ[H] and Nov(ℤ,H,N) are finite products of characteristic-zero fields, then build the period-order topology and cyclic-cover norms. These use the pushforward and domain results above.

frontier.name: Closed one-forms and period covers (N2)
frontier.text: : the zero locus, the Morse condition, the period homomorphism and the period-kernel cover. These depend on the DifferentialGeometry, MorseTheory and UniversalCovers suppliers rather than on anything built here.

status.glance: The algebraic foundations are well advanced. N1's period-controlled completion is nearly complete: Nov is a complete topological ring with functoriality, exp/log, infinite products and the Laurent comparison. N4's based scalar torsion now has multiplicativity and scalar extension. Every geometric layer (N2, N3, N5, N6, N7) is still untouched.

frontier.name: Cell attachment across a critical level
frontier.text: — glue the quadratic-model retraction into M through the admissible charts and combine it with the band deformation, giving M_{c+ε} ≃ M_{c−ε} ∪ D^λ relative to the lower sublevel.

frontier.name: Sublevels and bands as manifolds with boundary
frontier.text: — the regular-level atlas is in place, so what remains is the boundary atlases for M_a and f⁻¹[a,b] and the smooth version of the band product.

frontier.name: Lusternik–Schnirelmann corollaries (M4)
frontier.text: — the cup-length bound #Crit(f) ≥ cupLength + 1 needs AlgebraicTopology's categorical-cover supplement. The minimum c(M) needs a finite Morse witness, which waits on Morse approximation.

frontier.name: Morse approximation in the strong topology (M3)
frontier.text: — define strong C^k neighbourhoods, then run the compact-exhaustion perturbation argument. The smooth proper exhaustion it starts from is available.

frontier.name: The CW model and the strong Morse inequalities
frontier.text: — the sequence of regular sublevels for a proper bounded-below Morse function is proved ([`exists_regular_sublevel_exhaustion`](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Morse/Exhaustion.html#TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_regular_sublevel_exhaustion)), but both steps wait on cell attachment.

status.glance: The local theory, critical-free band deformation, regular levels as submanifolds, the Lusternik–Schnirelmann bound and gradient convergence with an exponential rate are all proved. Handle and cell attachment on a manifold, the CW model, Morse approximation, the Morse inequalities and Morse–Bott theory have not begun.

frontier.name: Orbits as homogeneous spaces (N0.3)
frontier.text: — construct the orbit as G/C_G(x), with tangent space [𝔤, x]. Its dimension count dim G − dim C_G(x) is already proved, so what remains is the quotient and the orbit map.

frontier.name: Internal Jordan decomposition (N0.2)
frontier.text: — show that the semisimple part of a Lie derivation is a derivation, and split x = xₛ + xₙ inside 𝔤 with uniqueness. Nothing for this has landed.

frontier.name: Weighted diagrams and finiteness (N2.2, N2.4)
frontier.text: — the open orbit of the grade-zero centralizer on 𝔤(2) and the injection of orbits into weighted diagrams. The {0, 1, 2} bound, [𝔤(0), e] = 𝔤(2) and the centralizer dimension formula are in hand. The open-orbit step needs the orbit dictionary above.

frontier.name: Type A partitions and dominance (N4)
frontier.text: — Jordan-chain bases, partitions from dim ker(Xᵏ), the centralizer dimension Σ(λ′ⱼ)², and explicit degenerations for the converse of the closure rank bounds.

frontier.name: The nilpotent cone as a scheme (N1)
frontier.text: — the zero fiber of the adjoint quotient χ, which consumes ReductiveGroups 11C and the FormalConnectionsOpers invariant adapter. N5 and N7–N9 wait on it.

status.glance: The Lie-algebraic theory of sl₂-triples is in place: Jacobson–Morozov, Kostant conjugacy, the transverse decomposition and the {0, 1, 2} bound. The Slodowy slice exists as an affine subspace with its contracting action. Group-level work has started with algebraic centralizers and their dimensions. There is still no internal Jordan decomposition and no nilpotent cone as a scheme. The flag variety, exponential, Springer resolution and subregular surfaces have not begun.

rows.name: NoncommutativeGeometry

frontier.name: The SBI sequence
frontier.text: — I and B on cohomology exist, and B ∘ I = 0. What remains is S as the exterior product with σ₁, followed by exactness at every term.

frontier.name: Algebraic K₀/K₁ and descent of the pairings
frontier.text: — build K₀ by group completion and K₁ as GL∞/E∞, then show both pairings factor through them. Stabilization and direct sums are already proved.

frontier.name: Periodic cyclic cohomology
frontier.text: — the direct limit under S, its comparison with the (b, B) totalization, and the pinned constants c₂ₘ and c₂ₖ₊₁.

frontier.name: Continuous cyclic cohomology
frontier.text: — the quotient of continuous cocycles by continuous coboundaries, with its quotient topology. It also needs the comparison with continuous functionals on completed tensors, and completed bar resolutions. N6's torus computation needs all of these.

frontier.name: Higher universal forms
frontier.text: — the graded differential algebra over A⁺ with d² = 0. The aim is to show that every cyclic cocycle is the character of a universal-form cycle, which now has the cycle-to-cocycle direction to build on.

status.glance: For unital algebras, the algebraic cyclic theory of N1 is mostly in place: the (b, B) operators, the comparison with the cyclic bicomplex, Hochschild cohomology, and cycles with their characters. SBI exactness, periodic cohomology and the higher universal forms are still missing. N2 has both of Connes' pairings, with their stabilization and invariance properties, but no K-theory for them to descend to. N3–N7 have not begun.

rows.name: OperatorAlgebraDynamics

frontier.name: The integrated form as a ⋆-representation
frontier.text: — prove (π⋊U)(f*) = (π⋊U)(f)*. Multiplicativity is already done, so this is the last step before the integrated form becomes a ⋆-homomorphism of the convolution algebra.

frontier.name: The twisted L¹ Banach ⋆-algebra
frontier.text: — prove that the twisted involution is L¹-isometric, complete C_c(G,A), and build approximate units compatible with those of A.

frontier.name: The full crossed product
frontier.text: — prove that the integrated regular representation of a faithful ρ is injective on C_c(G,A). Then define the full norm over a bounded family of cyclic representations, complete to `A⋊αG`, and prove its universal property into multiplier algebras.

frontier.name: The Gibbs state and ground states
frontier.text: — for a matrix Hamiltonian K, the unique β-KMS state is Tr(e^{−βK}·)/Tr(e^{−βK}), and the β → ∞ limits are ground states. Both build directly on the existing KMS and state-space API.

frontier.name: The KMS simplex and modular characterization
frontier.text: — show that extreme KMS states are exactly the factor states and that K_β is a Choquet simplex, and identify the modular flow with τ_{−βt}. These need the GNS normal extension and V10's modular operator, and are the heaviest remaining part of D7.

status.glance: Two layers have started. D1 has its convolution ⋆-algebra, a multiplicative integrated form and the regular covariant representation, but no completed crossed product yet. D7 has its basic KMS theory, including the dense criterion, invariance, and compactness and convexity of K_β, but none of the modular, simplex or ground-state theory. D2–D6 and D8–D9 have not begun.

frontier.name: Conjugacy of maximal tori.
frontier.text: The general theorem still assumes that diagonalizable subgroups conjugate into a reference torus. The vector-group step for solvable groups is in place: [two splittings of a semidirect product by a diagonalizable group are conjugate](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/SemidirectProduct.html#TauCeti.Comodule.IsRegularCocycle₁.isConj_pointSplitting).

frontier.name: Parabolics as `P(λ)`.
frontier.text: It remains to identify each parabolic `k`-subgroup with some `P(λ)` and to prove that `U(k)` acts transitively on Levi subgroups. [Distinct points of `U(λ)` already give distinct Levi factors](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Dynamic/Conjugation.html#BialgHom.injOn_conjugate_leviDefiningHopfIdeal). Layer 7b waits on this.

frontier.name: Root datum and Weyl group of a reductive group.
frontier.text: Centralizers of character kernels start the rank-one root maps. Extracting roots and coroots and identifying `N(T)/T` with the Weyl group remain.

frontier.name: Signed ADE folding.
frontier.text: Signed cycles contribute `A` or `A[2]`, and [orbit column sums of a forest's Cartan matrix are one or two](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/OrbitCartan.html#SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic.exists_graphCartanMatrix_sum_orbit). What remains is the pinned action on the Lie carrier, the integral fixed basis and bracket, and the folded presentation.

frontier.name: Projective closed orbits and Lang's theorem.
frontier.text: Layer 3A next needs properness of the orbit model and the equivariant restriction `V → H⁰(X, O(1))`. ReductiveGroupsPartII owns Lang's theorem, and nothing here yet applies it to `F`-stable parabolics, unipotent radicals or centralizers, so Layers 7b–7e cannot start.

status.glance: The foundations are done: the group-scheme dictionary, representations as comodules, the Lie algebra, tori and the unipotent radical. Borel conjugacy, closed orbits and Matsushima's affine quotient are proved in general. The structure theory beyond Borel conjugacy is partial. Most of the finite-field lane (Layers 7b–7e and 7g) has not begun, and neither have Levi complements in characteristic zero, classification or the spectral Weyl lane.

frontier.name: Tor′ vanishing for reflection groups
frontier.text: — build a graded free `A`-resolution of `k`, push `δ_s` and multiplication by `ℓ` through to `Tor′_1^A(k,S)`, and use Reynolds invariants on the resolution to show the group is zero. The divided-difference operator and the Hilbert ideal are ready for this.

frontier.name: Forward Shephard–Todd
frontier.text: — from Tor′ vanishing, deduce that `S` is free over `A`, then prove faithfully flat regularity descent and the vertex cotangent-dimension count. That gives polynomiality on `dim V` generators. The regularity-descent lemma is a separate target the README flags explicitly.

frontier.name: Reynolds and scalar extension
frontier.text: — show that the invariant subalgebra and the Reynolds projector commute with base change in the finite-free setting. This is the last named §1 construction, and §3 needs it to move degrees from ℝ to ℂ and from ℚ to ℝ.

frontier.name: Converse Shephard–Todd
frontier.text: — the inertia/stabilizer correspondence in codimension one, purity of the branch locus for the residual map `V/H → V/G`, and triviality of connected finite étale covers of affine space. None of these has been started.

frontier.name: Coinvariant package for real reflection groups
frontier.text: — the Jacobian as a product of reflecting-hyperplane forms, the harmonic complement, freeness of rank `|W|`, and the identities `∏ dᵢ = |W|` and `Σ dᵢ = r + |Ref(W)|`. All of this waits on polynomiality.

status.glance: Most of the finite-group invariant layer (§1) is done: the invariant subalgebra and Reynolds operator, Molien's formula, Noether's finiteness theorem and degree bound. Groundwork for the forward direction of Shephard–Todd has started, but neither direction of the theorem is proved. The real-reflection coinvariant package, the Weyl degree/Coxeter dictionary and the source examples have not begun.

frontier.text: — in odd dimension, show that flipping the line coordinate conjugates the spinor action by the parity involution, and that the two actions together give `Cliff ≅ End S × End S`. This is the last item of spin Layer 4.

status.glance: Of the roadmap, only the algebraic core of R1's curvature calculus is in substantial shape. The round sphere and upper half-space have been computed as constant-curvature models. I found nothing yet on Jacobi fields, index theory, comparison geometry, minimal submanifolds, Bochner identities or spherical harmonics.

frontier.name: Value group and power-bounded elements (§2.2)
frontier.text: — prove that some fixed power of `|f|sup` lies in `|K|`, and that `A° = {|f|sup ≤ 1}`, `A°° = {|f|sup < 1}` and `|f|sup = inf ‖fⁿ‖^(1/n)`. Maximum modulus, the prerequisite, is now proved.

frontier.name: Weak stability (Layer 0.2)
frontier.text: — prove that the Gauss fraction field is weakly stable and that normalisation is finite. This blocks the Japanese property in §1.2 and the Banach function algebra theorem in §2.2.

frontier.name: Fraction algebras (§1.4)
frontier.text: — construct Weierstrass, Laurent and rational fractions with their universal properties. They are the entry point to affinoid subdomains and to every later geometric layer.

frontier.name: Affinoid tensor products (§1.3)
frontier.text: — identify the pushout with `A⟨X,Y⟩/(I,J)`. The relative algebra and its universal property, which were the missing input, are now available.

frontier.name: The rest of §6.1
frontier.text: — continuous maps, induced G-topologies, the G0–G2 completeness results and pasting, on top of the new G-site.

status.glance: The basic algebra of affinoid algebras is in place: presentations, noetherianity, Noether normalisation, independence of the topology from the presentation, and now the maximum modulus principle and the heights of maximal ideals. Layer 2 is partial: the rest of its supremum-norm theory and all of the reduction theory remain. The geometry has only just begun, with the general definition of a G-topology and its site. Weak stability, fraction algebras, tensor products, affinoid spaces, Čech acyclicity, coherent cohomology and analytification have not begun.

frontier.text: — prove maximal-chain connectivity by rank-two replacements in parabolic Bruhat intervals, then the rank-two bond-gcd checks (A₁×A₁, A₂, B₂, G₂), then the a-chain divisibility criterion. The cover bonds it is built from are now available.

Nothing geometric exists yet: there are no flags, Schubert cells, Bott–Samelson schemes, line bundles, splittings, standard monomials or K-rings.

frontier.text: — compose the inverse Clifford map with Q₀ and prove q(uψ) = q(ψ), C(q(ψ))ψ = (|ψ|²/2)ψ, |q(ψ)|² = |ψ|⁴/8 and the transported derivative. The pointwise ingredients all exist.

frontier.text: — C*C = 4·Id and CC* = 4 times the trace-free projection, τ(Id) = 0, and τ landing in iΛ⁺ on self-adjoint endomorphisms.

frontier.name: Half-spin representations of Spinᶜ(4) (SW1.1)
frontier.text: — build ρ± on S±, prove descent, smoothness and det ρ± = z², and compare the native Spin(4) ≃ SU(2)×SU(2) factor labels with this Γ convention. This needs FourManifolds F4's Spinᶜ(n) quotient.

frontier.name: The smooth self-dual bundles Λ± (SW2.1)
frontier.text: — globalize the pointwise star through ComplexKahlerGeometry K5a's metric Hodge star. The roadmap is explicit that the algebraic star alone does not supply the bundle.

frontier.name: Geometric bundles and the determinant connection (SW1.2–SW1.3)
frontier.text: — associated bundles W±, the line L, the Spinᶜ connection and its curvature formula. These open the way to the Dirac and Weitzenböck work of SW3.

status.glance: The pointwise algebra of SW2 is largely in place: the rank-one quadratic endomorphism Q₀ with its derivative, and the chirality and self-duality algebra of an oriented four-space. Everything global is still to come: Spinᶜ bundles, connections, Dirac operators, gauge quotients, compactness, regularity, orientations, invariants and wall crossing.

frontier.name: Finish the Fock module (G1.2)
frontier.text: — the creation/annihilation anticommutators, adjointness of wedge and contraction for the exterior Gram metric, skew-Hermitian c(v), and the 2^p factor between the native and normalized metrics.

frontier.name: Positive Hermitian spinor metric (G1.3)
frontier.text: — existence of a metric making ρ a *-representation for `conjStar`, transported from the Fock metric, and uniqueness up to a positive scalar via Schur. The Morita evaluation now supplies the multiplicity spaces; the existence proof needs the metric half of G1.2.

frontier.name: Complex positivity of the trace (G1.3)
frontier.text: — τ_ℂ(a*a) = Σ|a_I|²·Π b(e_i, e_i) ≥ 0 on the tensor complexification, and the null set as the ideal generated by the radical of b.

frontier.name: Odd-dimensional labelled factors (G1.4)
frontier.text: — the central element ω_ℂ, its idempotents, and ψ(ω_ℂ) = −Γ through the Cl(V) ≃ Cl⁰(V ⊕ ℝ) dictionary that is now in place.

frontier.name: Volume and chirality (G2.1)

Nothing geometric has begun: there are no chirality comparisons (G2), Clifford bundles (G3), spin structures (G4), spinor bundles (G5) or Dirac operators (G6).

rows.name: TauberianBoundaryConvergence

frontier.name: Laplace transform of the step function
frontier.text: — define `f(t) = a ⌊eᵗ⌋₊` for `t ≥ 0`, prove it is locally integrable using the step partition, and identify its transform on `Re z > 0` with `F(z+1) + H(z)` from `LSeriesHasSum`.

frontier.name: `boundedDirichlet_tendsto_ordered_at_one`
frontier.text: — apply Newman's theorem at `T = log(N+1)`, identify the finite integral with `Σ_{n≤N} a n log(1 + 1/n)`, and subtract the step correction at `0`. The result must be stated as the ordered limit of `Σ_{1≤n≤N} a n / n`.

frontier.name: N2 comparison API
frontier.text: — the real-to-natural cutoff equivalence, finite coefficient changes with explicit corrections, linearity and uniqueness of the endpoint.

frontier.name: N3 coefficients and Euler logarithm
frontier.text: — define `aχ = χ · Λ / log`, prove its values on prime powers and the bound `‖aχ‖ ≤ 1`, and glue local logarithms of `LFunction χ` on balls along `Re s = 1` into a holomorphic extension of the Euler log. This needs N2's endpoint before it can be used.

frontier.name: Ordered Euler product at `1`
frontier.text: — the `Tendsto` of the finite products `∏_{p≤N} (1 − χ(p)/p)⁻¹` to `LFunction χ 1`, plus the finite-deletion variant. Both wait on the item above.

status.glance: N1, the bounded-complex Newman Tauberian theorem, is done. N2, the ordered Dirichlet-series endpoint at `s = 1`, is partial: only its holomorphic step correction exists. N3, the Dirichlet-character Euler-product comparison, has not begun.

frontier.name: Degree-m vortex operator (TG4).
frontier.text: Use the vacuum inverse as an exterior parametrix at a vortex in its winding-m end trivialization, and prove Fredholmness, cokernel vanishing and real index 2m. This first needs the affine field space A_m^k, the Banach gauge group G_(k+1) and the deformation complex.

frontier.name: Four-twist labels from geometry (TG2, TG11.1).
frontier.text: Define σ and i by determinant transport from the twisted normal operators, so that the local-zeta-factor identity applies to actual orbit tori. This needs TG1's embedded normal operator and the HF determinant conventions.

frontier.name: Disjointness on a square-zero ray.
frontier.text: Prove that distinct relevant torus images on the ray of A₀ are disjoint, so that the ray expansion becomes the count.

frontier.name: Weighted count at fixed J (TG3).
frontier.text: Instantiate `IsGoodCycle` from actual curves (positivity, singular adjunction, generic-point bounds), then build the finite configuration carrier and Gr_(J,ω)(A). This needs bounded-window compactness and AnalyticStableMaps.

frontier.name: The integrated product energy identity (TG10.2).
frontier.text: Integrate the pointwise identity against the product Dirac splitting to get 0 = ‖∇_Tψ‖² + ‖B_A⁺ψ‖² + ‖ι_T F_A‖² + 2π²⟨l², [X]⟩, first for smooth solutions and then for Sobolev ones.

status.glance: Algebra and the first model analysis are in place, and nothing geometric is. That covers the four-twist weights and the ray expansion (TG2), the intersection-lattice algebra of good cycles (TG3, TG6.2), the vacuum operator of the plane vortex model (TG4), and several normalization identities for the product application (TG10.2, TG11.1, TG11.2). Embedded normal operators, compactness, degree-m vortices, large-r estimates, gluing and the SW = Gr point equality have not begun.

frontier.text: — define `H_n(q)` by generators and relations, prove the `T_w` basis indexed by `Sₙ`, and prove that `H_n(q)` is isomorphic to the stage and injects into the infinite algebra. Almost everything else in H1 is blocked on this.

frontier.text: — uniqueness is done. The library's own documentation says existence waits on the basis theorem for the stages.

frontier.name: Jucys-Murphy elements and their tableau eigenvalues
frontier.text: — the content-separation input is ready. What remains is the elements themselves, their commutation, and the eigenvalue `Q^(column−row)` on a fixed Specht basis, which needs the Specht modules first.

frontier.name: The cocenter basis and Ram's formula
frontier.text: — `cycleBlock_cocenterBasis` and the trace-comparison exports. The power-sum basis covers the symmetric-function side, but the Hecke side has not been started.

frontier.name: Atomic tensor models
frontier.text: — the signed R-matrix exists, but the weighted trace on it, and the proof that it gives a positive Markov trace, are open. These need the H3 state carrier to be specified first.

status.glance: The foundations of H1 have started. The infinite Hecke algebra, its stages and its braid homomorphism are in place, and so are the content-separation and power-sum inputs to the module theory. None of H1's main theorems are proved yet: there is no finite presentation, no basis theorem, no Specht modules and no cocenter basis. H2 has uniqueness of Markov traces but not existence. frontier.name: The conformal Laplacian's operator identity and the Yamabe quotient
frontier.text: — prove L_ĝ(v) = u^(−(n+2)/(n−2))L_g(uv), integrate by parts to the energy form, define Q_g and prove Q_ĝ(v) = Q_g(uv). The pointwise scalar law is now present. The weak-domain statement waits on Y1's Sobolev carrier.

frontier.name: The converse of Weyl–Schouten
frontier.text: — show that W = 0 (n ≥ 4) or C = 0 (n = 3) implies local conformal flatness, through the first-jet system Hess f = P + df⊗df − |df|²g/2 and local Frobenius. This first needs the Cotton conformal law and div W = (n−3)C.

frontier.name: Critical points of the quotient
frontier.text: — identify critical points of Q with weak solutions of L_g u = λ|u|^(p_n−2)u. The integrated Yamabe equation gives the smooth positive case of λ = Q at unit norm.

frontier.name: The sharp Euclidean Sobolev inequality
frontier.text: — with the extremals' energy computed, what remains is a_n∫|du|² ≥ Y(Sⁿ)‖u‖²_{p_n} on D¹,² and the classification of its equality cases (Y2.1–Y2.2).

frontier.text: — Y1's H¹/Lᵖ adapters, compact embeddings and the first eigenvalue of L_g. These depend on the PDE and K5a supplier lanes.

frontier.text: Each braid functor now descends to derived categories. What remains is to transport the inverse and braid relations to obtain the Artin action there, as the roadmap asks.

frontier.text: In Tau Ceti's sign conventions the displayed `m₄` is formal, so that target needs restating. A single-rotation loop operation is the natural replacement, but no result yet shows the resulting deformation is not formal.

frontier.text: Only recognition is proved, with circles and tori as examples; constructing one rests on realization theory the README places outside this roadmap.

frontier.name: Bases without a universal cover.
frontier.text: The standing local hypotheses are shown to be exactly what a simply connected cover requires, so the classification cannot be pushed further as stated; spaces failing them would need a different notion of cover, and nothing here attempts one.

status.glance: Every stage of the roadmap has its stated targets proved. The universal cover is constructed, subgroups of `π₁(X, x₀)` classify connected covers in pointed and unpointed form, covers are classified categorically with `π₁(X, x₀)` recovered as the automorphisms of the fibre functor, and the applications (`π₁(S¹)`, `π_n(S¹)`, tori, `K(G, 1)` recognition, `RPⁿ`) are complete. What remains lies beyond the roadmap's text.
